item.title: RemoteControl.ZMQ v1.5.5.38
item.description:
Product: RemoteControl.ZMQ v1.5.5.38
Company: LevyLab
Release Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:49:52 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: Override library implementing ZMQ lazy pirate reliable request reply (RRR) protocal using RemoteControl SMO framework.

Release Notes: ### 1.5.5

A server (REP) now replies to a request that is not valid JSON instead of leaving the socket stuck (#9). The reply is a JSON-RPC 2.0 error: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"Parse error"}}`. A request that is valid JSON but malformed (for example, missing or with an empty `method`) gets `-32600 Invalid Request`. In both cases the server keeps answering the requests that follow, so no restart is needed. Before this, a non-JSON request got no reply, and REQ/REP lockstep kept the server from answering anything else.

- Parse Request returns -32600 "Invalid Request" when "method" is missing or empty.

item.title: JSON-RPC v1.2.8.17
item.description:
Product: JSON-RPC v1.2.8.17
Company: PRIrvin
Release Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 21:16:33 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: Library for encoding and decoding JSON-RPC 2.0 request and response objects

https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification

Release Notes: JSON-RPC 1.2.8

Fixed
Instrument errors are no longer sent as a bare null (PRIrvin/JSON-RPC#2). Until now, Create Response.vi produced a real error reply only for the reserved JSON-RPC codes (-32700, -32600, -32603..-32601, -32099..-32000). Any other code, such as the Instrument Framework’s 4001 “command not supported”, 5402, or DAQmx errors, went out as the literal null with no envelope. Every error code now produces a standard reply:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":4001,"message":"command not supported"},"id":"1"}

The message is the LabVIEW error’s source text. Codes are sent as they are; 4001 is not remapped to -32601.

Behavior change
Clients that used to get an empty result with no error for an unsupported or failed command will now get an error. LabVIEW clients (Parse Response.vi, RemoteControl.ZMQ) return it on error out with the original code. Python clients get an error member instead of None. Check scripts that relied on the old silent result.

Tests
New UNITTEST-JSON-RPC-Error-Object.vi, added to UNITTESTS.vi. It covers non-reserved, DAQmx and reserved codes, the no-error and notification (id “-1”) cases, and a Create Response / Parse Response round trip.

Upgrading
Instrument Type and RemoteControl.ZMQ accept this version without being rebuilt.
Multichannel-Lockin: its ApplyMe_2.23.0.vipc pins JSON-RPC 1.2.6.15 exactly, so regenerate it with 1.2.8.
Instrument executables (lock-in, KH7008, Transport Server) must be rebuilt to include the fix.

Known issue
A request that isn’t valid JSON still gets no reply, which leaves the server’s ZMQ REP socket stuck until the instrument is restarted. The fix is planned mainly in RemoteControl.ZMQ. Don’t send malformed requests to running instruments.
item.dc:creator: PRIrvin

item.title: Instrument Framework v1.15.14.56
item.description:
Product: Instrument Framework v1.15.14.56
Company: LevyLab
Release Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:00:57 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: An object-oriented framework based on JKI SMOs, developed by the LevyLab at the University of Pittsburgh.

An Instrument developed using this framework will have the access to the following capabilities:

- Framework for communicating with hardware (Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL))
- Periodically polls the instrument for its settings and logs them to a PGSQL database
- Defines an API to allow external programs to control compiled instances of the application and remotely across a network (Either NI's Simple Messaging Library (STM) (deprecated in v1.9) or cross-platform protocol ZMQ (preferred beginning with v1.9))
- Provide a user interface (optional but probably desirable).
- Methods for reading and writing configuration from disk.

Release Notes: [1.15.14]
#201 Open SMO.vi tests for existing connection and preserves connection if one already exists
